A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work. Their complete main texts, equations, Algorithm 1, and Appendices A–B are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports theoretical constructions, impossibility bounds, accuracy guarantees, and proofs. Neither the main text nor the appendices report original empirical results.

after.justification: v2 remains entirely theoretical. Its added subsampling analysis is a mathematical proof, not an experimental or simulation result.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 retains its query generation, score updates, and final query. The Laplace mechanism in Section 4 is unchanged. Extending the attack's analysis to subsampling does not change its procedure.

E1.justification: Neither version uses empirical training or evaluation datasets or tasks. The subsampling extension concerns a theoretical mechanism class, not added evaluation coverage.

E2.justification: Neither version reports evaluated baseline comparisons. Subsampling is newly covered by the impossibility theorem, rather than introduced as an experimental comparator.

E3.justification: Neither version contains experimental protocols. The new subsampling definition and revised bounded-output assumptions specify the theoretical setting, not evaluation procedures.

E4.justification: Neither version reports ablations, empirical robustness tests, or case studies. The added proof case belongs to the theoretical contribution.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated experiments, seeds, confidence intervals, or statistical tests. Their probability bounds are theoretical guarantees.

E6.justification: There are no empirical result entries in either version. Existing quantitative bounds remain unchanged; their extended theoretical applicability is assessed under T1 and C1.

T1.justification: Definitions 2.1–2.2 formalize noise-addition and fresh, with-replacement subsampling mechanisms. Lemma 3.3 gains a subsampling derivation establishing the same expected score increment, extending Theorems 1.4 and 3.5 to this additional class. Section 2 also revises bounded-output assumptions and explicitly states the zero-mean assumption already used in v1's proof. Section 4 and Appendices A–B retain their mathematics.

C1.justification: Section 1.1.1 broadens the central linear-query impossibility claim from noise-addition mechanisms to the defined Noise and Subsampling family. This substantially extends the negative contribution's scope; the positive-result claim remains unchanged.

C2.justification: The stated implication for future algorithms now excludes subsampling as well as noise addition as routes around the barrier. Section 2 replaces the clipping/negligible-tail discussion with explicit output ranges and explains why answers outside [-1, 2] already constitute accuracy failures.

D1.justification: Neither version supplies implementation resources, code or data access, hardware, or runtime information. The added sampling specifications define the theorem's mechanism class rather than document an implementation.

R1.justification: Section 1.1.1 newly positions noise addition and subsampling together as covering all known efficient polynomial-time techniques supporting superlinear query counts in the independent setting. The cited works and remaining prior-work discussion are unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 introduces NS terminology, expands the preliminaries and proof exposition locally, corrects several wording and notation slips, and updates funding text. The overall section and appendix organization remains intact.

P2.justification: Algorithm 1 retains its display format but now precedes the attack analysis instead of interrupting Lemma 3.2's proof. Other layout differences are primarily text and equation reflow; no figures or result tables are added.

improvement.justification: The added subsampling proof in Lemma 3.3 closes a substantial gap in the central impossibility result: v1 addressed noise addition, while v2 also rules out the explicitly defined subsampling alternative at the same query bound. This materially broadens the theoretical contribution, supported by a derivation and clearer assumptions, while preserving the positive analysis and appendix proofs.
